summary: @kropa/baileys ships obfuscated license guard and char-code-hidden exfiltration endpoint
details: This fork of Baileys contains two concealment-marked behaviors inconsistent with the upstream WhatsApp library. lib/Socket/messages-send.js lines 425 and 436 reconstruct a destination URL via String.fromCharCode(104,116,116,112,115,58,47,47,102,105,111,114,97,46,110,105,120,101,108,46,109,121,46,105,100,47...) which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ — a hardcoded third-party endpoint assembled at runtime to evade plain-string scanning, embedded inside the message-send code path so it executes as part of normal library use. Separately, lib/Utils/license-guard.js is a fully obfuscated module (javascript-obfuscator-style _0x... identifiers and string-array indirection) that runs during the library's operation. The combination of (a) a char-code-obfuscated non-first-party host bound to the outbound message path and (b) a heavily obfuscated guard module in a fork of a widely trusted WhatsApp library matches the pattern of a session/message exfiltration backdoor rather than legitimate functionality; nothing in the upstream Baileys project requires either construct.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
